rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable annual rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage, and the landlord can no longer add an extra percentage increase for utilities. Rent may be raised to market rate when the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for specified reasons, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. This includes apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwelling units on the same parcel, hotel/motel/rooming/boarding house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks.
rules.exemptions: For condominiums and townhomes, rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. A landlord can apply for a luxury exemption by establishing the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: RSO additional tenant rent increase
rules.requirement: A 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is allowed for an additional tenant who is not a dependent, and the landlord must make it within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for an additional tenant (not a dependent)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units).
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction, notice and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenancies may be ended only for listed at-fault reasons (such as failure to pay rent, lease violations, nuisance or damage, or illegal use) or no-fault reasons (such as owner or family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition, government order, or conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict, a 30-day and 60-day written notice, and payment of relocation assistance. Termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service.
rules.key_value: 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension); relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units).
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO); Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).
